final_test_status: At most one unused IDSSE match remains; two new final matches are required. No final evaluation or promotion in this experiment. Verify WR9 prior use before accessing it. No final labels are opened by the driver.
basis: Controlled-only diagnosis on development: 125 of 279 missed phases shorter than 2 s have a correct isolated H/A/D winner on a strict majority of their frames. This is association, not proof of a decoder cause. 26 of all 301 short phases are below the unchanged 8-frame internal minimum duration.
hypothesis: A destination-specific discount for credible control evidence can recover short phases suppressed by fixed switching costs without adding unsupported flicker.
change: Keep controlled emissions, minimum duration and D costs identical. For H->A or A->H at destination frame t, use base_cost * (1 - (2/3)*clip((destination_score - max(other_team_score,dead_score) - 0.75)/1.25,0,1)). Cost is 4..12 at the fixed base cost 12. Scores are uncalibrated evidence, not probabilities. No future reference or identity input.
parameter_basis: One bounded engineering hypothesis: require a positive margin over both competing states; full discount at margin 2 within the existing geometry range. No sweep, no threshold fitting to candidate scores.
timing: One warm-up per method, then three alternating measured predict-only runs; deep copies and data loading excluded. Check deterministic label hashes on every repetition.
stopping_rule: Evaluate this candidate once on development after software tests. If any gate fails, reject and stop this experiment; do not retune or relax gates. If all pass, leave experimental pending two new final matches. Do not run competition public scoring or select using consumed final results.
diagnostic_scope: Native 25-Hz complete development matches; official score grid separates metadata periods. Report all IoUs, TP/FP/FN, frame macroF1, D recall, transition F1 and short-phase diagnostics. No manual labels or competition reference inputs.
limitations: Repeated use of two development games risks overfitting. Same-provider tracking has no missing-ball frames in these games. Synthetic missingness tests are software/robustness evidence only. No claim of generalisation or significance.
